summary: Units 34-66 (33 units) reviewed against the Sanskrit. 1 error, 18 minor; all patched. The draft is sound: splits, sandhi and compound analysis are right throughout; the text_flag at 42 (na-ity -> na-iti) is confirmed (ity cannot stand before k-; 34/52/58 read na-iti). The draft author's doubts: 40 'bhaya' governing the five preceding members is the better reading and the alternative is honestly noted; 'din' = diṅ is right but is an e-text anomaly (it writes dig. elsewhere), so it now gets a text_flag; 45 'asataś cārjanam' literal reading kept, English aligned to the literal Hindi; 46 'anitya-yānam' left open in English but the Hindi had silently chosen one sense, now literal; 51 the dot in rājahite.niyoktum is a markup slip, now a text_flag, 'avasrāvayitum' acceptable; 63 'ekeṣām' gloss made literal; 64 'asat-pragraha' aligned with 65. The supplied predicate '(is the more serious)' in 47/55/62 is correct and bracketed in English, as in chunk 1 units 24/30; it is unmarked in Hindi, as chunk 1 also does. One real grammar error (59 bāhyeṣu labelled f.). Consistency: this chunk used 'अधिक भारी' for garīyas where chunk 1 of this chapter uses 'अधिक गम्भीर' (fixed in 39/47/55/62). Not patched, for a person: the Hindi quoting style (straight quotes + em dash here, curly quotes + comma in chunk 1) and 'So it is said.' for a closing iti (41/51/57; chunk 1 of 8.3 just closes the quote, chunk 1 of 8.1 writes 'so ends the view') are cosmetic and could be unified chapter-wide. No regrouping suggested. Glossary extended with the 8.3 terms (vyasana = vice in 8.3 vs calamity in 8.1, garīyas, tantra, the four kāmaja vices, asat-pragraha, saṅgha).
